definitions.explanation: A line made up of connected straight segments that change direction at each point. Most commonly encountered in the term {折|お}れ{線|せん}グラフ (line graph).

examples.japanese: {折|お}れ{線|せん}グラフを{作|つく}る。
{気温|きおん}の{変化|へんか}を{折|お}れ{線|せん}グラフで{表|あらわ}した。
examples.english: I showed the temperature changes in a line graph.

examples.japanese: {折|お}れ{線|せん}グラフを{見|み}ると、{売上|うりあげ}が{年々|ねんねん}{増加|ぞうか}していることが{分|わ}かる。
examples.english: Looking at the line graph, you can see that sales have been increasing year by year.

notes:
Most commonly used in the compound {折|お}れ{線|せん}グラフ (line graph), which is one of the basic graph types taught in Japanese elementary school math. The literal meaning is 'bent line' or 'broken line.'

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {折|お}れ{線|せん}グラフ: line graph
- {折|お}れ{線|せん}グラフで{示|しめ}す: to show with a line graph
- {折|お}れ{線|せん}グラフを{読|よ}み{取|と}る: to read a line graph

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {直線|ちょくせん}: straight line — a line without any bends
- {曲線|きょくせん}: curve — a smoothly curved line
- {棒|ぼう}グラフ: bar graph — another common graph type
- {円|えん}グラフ: pie chart — another common graph type

USAGE:
In Japanese math education, students learn the four basic graph types: {折|お}れ{線|せん}グラフ (line graph), {棒|ぼう}グラフ (bar graph), {円|えん}グラフ (pie chart), and {帯|おび}グラフ (stacked bar chart).
